title: A micromechanical cell stretching device compatible with super-resolution microscopy and single protein tracking
protocol: Pre-cut an elastomer Gel-Pak frame (40 μm) to the size of the glass coverslip using the Graphtec Cutting Plotter.
Mix PDMS and curing agent in a 10:1 ratio.
Centrifuge the mixture for 5 min at 2500 rpm to remove air bubbles.
Spin the PDMS on a silicon wafer to achieve a final thickness of 10 μm.
Pre-cure the PDMS for 25 min at 70°C.
Place the pre-cut Gel-Pak frame in contact with the 10 μm thick PDMS layer.
Curate the assembly overnight at 70°C.
Cut around the Gel-Pak frame using a blunt pair of scissors and gently detach the PDMS substrate from the wafer.
Plasma clean 24x40 mm glass coverslips.
Spin coat each slide with glycerol to form a uniform layer ∼0.7 μm thick.
Plasma clean the PDMS substrate for 1 minute on the side that will glide on the glycerol layer.
Lay the PDMS substrate onto the glycerol-coated coverslip immediately after plasma cleaning.
Design the fixed (holding) arm, the mobile (stretching) arm and the clamp composing the device on a CAD software.
Export the files (.obj or any 3D printing compatible format) and upload them onto PreForm software.
Set layer thickness to intermediate or small in PreForm software to avoid imperfections in the final structure.
Recommend using Grey Pro resin for high precision, moderate elongation, and low creep.
Cut glass coverslips in small parts with high precision knife.
Attach small glass parts to holding and stretching arm using superglue or Dow Corning™ High-Vacuum Grease.
Stick double sided tape to the glass parts on the holding and stretching arm.
Place the glass-PDMS assembly inside the clamp.
Attach the glass-PDMS assembly to the holding arm.
Attach the stretching arm to the glass-PDMS assembly using double-sided tape.
Culture actively dividing immortalized MEFs in DMEM supplemented medium in 75 cm² flasks.
Detach cells with trypsin/EDTA solution (1.5 mL).
Inactivate trypsin immediately after detachment by adding serum-containing DMEM (5 ml).
Count cells and adjust cell suspension volume to keep 1–2 million cells per tube per experimental condition.
Centrifuge cells at 300 × g for 5 min.
Resuspend the cell pellet in transfection reagent.
Mix the resuspended cells with DNA plasmids.
For sptPALM experiments, co-transfect cells with DNAs encoding for the protein of interest (3–5 μg per condition) and GFP-coupled reporter of the structure of interest (1–2 μg per condition).
For STED experiments, if necessary, transfect cells with a GFP-coupled reporter of the structure of interest (1–2 μg per condition).
Electroporate the cells using the Nucleofector™ 2b Device with the MEF T-020 program.
Replate the electroporated cells in a 6-well plate (about 0.3 million cells/well) in preheated culture medium and place them in a 37 °C incubator with humidified air containing 5% CO2.
Cover the micromechanical device with 10 μg/ml fibronectin solution (500-750 µl per device) and incubate at 37 °C for 1 to 1.5 hours.
Discard the fibronectin solution and wash 4-5 times with PBS.
Wash cells twice with PBS after removing the culture medium.
Incubate cells with trypsin–EDTA solution (0.3 ml per well) for 1–3 min at 37 °C for detaching cells.
Inactivate trypsin with trypsin inactivation medium (1 ml per well).
Centrifuge at 300 ×g for 5 min.
Resuspend cells in warm Ringer medium (1–2 ml).
Allow cells to recover for 20-30 min inside the incubator at 37 °C with 5% CO2.
Spread the cells on the device under a density of 70000-80000 cells per device.
Prepare a 1:500 solution of TetraSpeck™ 0.1 µm fluorescent beads in warm Ringer solution.
Add 200-300 µL of bead solution to each device to adsorb fluorescent beads on the substrate.
Mount the piezoelectric motor on a custom holder adapted to the microscope stage.
Mount the holder on the microscope.
Connect the piezoelectric motor controller and launch the PI Mikro Motor software.
Mount the micromechanical device on the stage-adapted holder.
Attach the stretching arm to the linear stage with a screw.
Adjust focus to the 3x3 mm observation 10 µm PDMS chamber.
Test whether the device is working properly by selecting a region with a good density of fluorescent beads and acquiring a snapshot before stretching.
Measure the distance between two beads in the same horizontal axis (D_before).
Apply a test stretching by displacing the linear stage of the piezoelectric motor while keeping the same region in focus, either manually or with a custom-written Metamorph routine.
Take another snapshot after the stretching and measure again the distance between the same two beads (D_after).
If D_after is larger than D_before, then the device is working properly.
Select a cell and launch a PALM acquisition at high frequency (50 Hz) for the entire field of observation.
Stretch by displacing the linear stage of the piezoelectric motor several hundred frames after initiating the acquisition.
Compensate for XY displacements using manual repositioning or automated stage repositioning during stretching.
Maintain the cell in the field of observation throughout the process.
Allow the plateau phase to last for 8-12 seconds before relaxation.
Select cells for imaging with most focal adhesions aligned parallel to the stretching axis.
Position cells closer to the holding arm in the micromechanical device.
Acquire an image of the GFP reporter before PALM acquisition.
Launch a high-frequency PALM acquisition at 50 Hz for 4000 frames.
Perform large stretching (10-50%) while tracking cell displacement with dichroic and emission filters.
Acquire an image of the GFP reporter after stretching is completed.
Launch another sptPALM acquisition post-stretching.
Perform live labelling of the target protein on the micromechanical device.
Wash the staining solution after labelling.
Incubate the device in warm Ringer solution until the experiment.
Select a cell and acquire a confocal image followed by a STED image on a sub region of the cell.
Stretch the cell according to the desired percentage.
Compensate for XY displacements using manual repositioning.
Warm 4% PFA with 0.25% Glutaraldehyde at 37°C.
Acquire several low resolution images of GFP markers for different cells after mounting the micromechanical device on the microscope.
Remove the entire module (device and motor in the stage-adapted holder) and stretch the cells outside the microscope.
Immediately after stretching, remove the Ringer solution and fix the cells in warm 4% PFA with 0.25% Glutaraldehyde.
Rinse fixed cells 3-4 times with PBS.
Clamp the stretching arm to the holding arm using the thread and groove system and two M3 screws.
Remove the screw that connects the stretching arm to the motor after clamping.
Label target proteins according to the imaging technique.
Label cells for DNA-PAINT imaging.
Acquire low resolution images of GFP markers before super-resolution imaging.
Immerse cells in Buffer C at 25°C for imaging.
Visualize Cy3B-labelled strands using a 561 nm laser.
Collect fluorescence with dichroic Di01-R561 and emission filter FF01-617/73.
Use ORCA-Flash4.0 sCMOS camera in streaming mode at 6.7 Hz.
Image Vimentin-GFP with GFP filter cube (excitation: FF01-472/30, dichroic: FF-495Di02, emission: FF02-520/28).
Perform super-resolution DNA-PAINT reconstruction and drift correction using Picasso software.
Dilute imager strand in Buffer C for visualization.
Incubate micromechanical device with 200-300 µL of 90 nm gold nanoparticles diluted in PBS (1:5 ratio) at RT for 15 min.
Wash the device three times with PBS and once with Buffer C.
Add imager strands to the stretching chamber until reaching an ideal density of blinking events.
Visualize vimentin-Halo with Cy3B-labelled DNA imager strands added at variable concentrations (2-5 nM).
Image cells at 25°C in PBS 1X using a microscope equipped with a WLL2 laser and a 775 nm depletion laser.
